figures.bridge_line: the bishop across the sea who would not concede the point - this world's most serious outside interlocutor, whose objections to the Hebrew-first project reach us in his own words

dates.floruit: bishop of Hippo from 395/396; Jerome's correspondent across roughly twenty-five years - pressing, in his own hand, the case against abandoning the Septuagint's received authority, and reporting the Oea congregation's revolt over one changed word in Jonah

figures.bridge_line: Paula's eldest daughter, dead at about twenty within months of taking up severe fasting - the death that turned Rome against the circle and set the 385 departure in motion

dates.born: c. 364 (modern reconstruction; she was about twenty at her death)
dates.died: 384, Rome - within months of adopting severe ascetic discipline after a young widowhood; at her funeral the crowd's anger turned on the monks, per Jerome's own report

figures.bridge_line: the pope whose commission began the translation work and whose protection made Rome possible - and whose death, in the same season as Blaesilla's, ended both

dates.floruit: bishop of Rome 366-384; commissioned Jerome's revision of the Latin Gospels and employed him as secretary and scriptural adviser from 382; his death removed the clerical protection that had made Jerome's Roman position tenable

figures.bridge_line: the daughter vowed to virginity from her youth - dedicatee of the world's most famous letter, and after her mother's death, head of the Bethlehem women's community to the world's own end

dates.born: c. 368 (modern reconstruction from Ep. 22's address to her as a young virgin in 384)
dates.died: 418, 419, or 420 - contested across a three-year window depending on the reference consulted; never resolved to a single year in this record set
dates.floruit: Rome until 385 (consecrated virgin from youth, the addressee of Ep. 22); Bethlehem 386-death; head of the women's community after Paula's death in 404

figures.bridge_line: the Roman who had divorced and remarried, did public penance, and then spent her fortune gathering the sick in from the streets - the network's Rome-based charitable founder, never a Bethlehem resident

dates.died: 399 or 400 - contested; this record does not pick
dates.floruit: Rome, of the gens Fabia: divorced a vicious first husband and remarried while he lived; after her second husband's death performed public penance; founded the hospital (nosocomium) for the sick in Rome; visited Bethlehem in 395 (the stay cut short amid fear of a Hunnic invasion); with Pammachius founded the travelers' hospice at Portus; her funeral drew crowds through Rome

figures.bridge_line: the scholar at the world's center - translator, letter-writer, and fierce disputant, whose authority rested on learning and patronage, never on office, and whose hand wrote nearly everything this world left behind

dates.born: c. 331 (Kelly) or c. 347 (Rebenich) - contested between the two standard modern reconstructions; this record does not pick
dates.died: 420 (year Widely Accepted); the traditional day, 30 September, rests on liturgical feast tradition and Prosper's chronicle, not a contemporary record - Inferential-Thin
dates.floruit: Rome 382-385 (secretary and scriptural adviser to Damasus; the Aventine circle); Bethlehem 386-420 (the monastery, the translation project, the controversies)

names.name: Eusebius Hieronymus (Jerome of Stridon, c. 331 or c. 347 - 420)

figures.bridge_line: the widow of the Aventine - the circle's founder before Jerome ever arrived, and after he left, the one in Rome to whom clergy brought their hardest scripture questions

dates.born: c. 325/330 (modern reconstruction; no source gives a year)
dates.died: 410, Rome - shortly after the Gothic sack, following rough treatment in her own house (Ep. 127; no independent corroboration)
dates.floruit: the Aventine household from her early widowhood (ascetic commitment from the 340s, the household as a multi-woman formation site best placed 360s-370s - modern reconstruction); after 385, per Ep. 127, a standing point of scriptural reference for Roman clergy until her death

figures.bridge_line: the senator turned monk - Paula's son-in-law, Rome's receiving-end for Jerome's fiercest defenses, and co-founder with Fabiola of the harbor hospice

dates.died: c. 409/410, Rome (modern reconstruction; before or during the sack's season)
dates.floruit: Roman senator, Paula's son-in-law (husband of her daughter Paulina); after Paulina's death (c. 396/397) took the monk's profession while remaining in Rome; with Fabiola founded the travelers' hospice at Portus; the standing addressee of Jerome's most consequential defenses (Ep. 57, the Apology)

figures.bridge_line: the widow whose fortune and resolve built Bethlehem - founder and head of the women's community, mother of Eustochium and Blaesilla, the material foundation of the whole scholarly project

dates.died: 404, Bethlehem - Ep. 108 dates her death precisely and gives her age; buried by the Church of the Nativity
dates.floruit: Rome until 385 (widowed 379/380, ascetic under Marcella's circle's influence); the 385-386 journey; Bethlehem 386-404 (founder and head of the women's community)

figures.bridge_line: the granddaughter vowed from the cradle - the child whose alphabet was designed by letter from Bethlehem, and who, still young, co-signed the community's report of the fire

dates.born: c. 397/400, Rome (approximate - Ep. 107 addresses her infancy c. 403)
dates.floruit: vowed to virginity from birth by her parents Laeta and Toxotius (Paula's son); the subject of Ep. 107's education program; at Bethlehem by 416, when she and her aunt Eustochium reported the attack to Pope Innocent

figures.bridge_line: the oldest friend who became the fiercest opponent - fellow translator of Origen, whose preface recalling Jerome's earlier admiration of the master set off the rupture neither man ever repaired

dates.died: 411, Sicily, in flight from the Gothic invasion
dates.floruit: Jerome's close friend from their student days; monastic founder on the Mount of Olives with Melania the Elder; translator of Origen into Latin - whose Peri Archon preface (397), describing without naming Jerome as Origen's earlier translator, ignited the public rupture; the exchange of Apologies 401-403
